$about: React Aria's state-attribute vocabulary mapped to Base UI's, measured per component by rendering rather than read off a docs page, plus the count of selector rewrites the migration costs. Branch experiment/base-ui, @base-ui/react@1.7.0.
question: The audit established that the verdict's 'no focus ring on switch or checkbox' and 'an ON toggle looks identical to an OFF one' were artifacts of the experiment's frozen-selector control, not Base UI defects. This file answers what unfreezing them actually costs, and what that extrapolates to across all 77 components.

vocabulary_discovery: Rendered each of the thirteen rebuilt components in each visual state under jsdom and dumped EVERY attribute of EVERY element. Raw: probe.state-vocabulary.json.

Where two candidate attributes could not be told apart from a single render — a selected tab versus the roving-focus cursor, a dragging slider thumb — rendered a second, disambiguating case. Raw: probe2.state-vocabulary.json.
Cross-checked every claim of ABSENCE against a grep of the installed dist, because a state that a render did not happen to trigger is not the same as a state that does not exist.
counting: experiments/harness/count-state-selectors.mjs diffs the React Aria baseline (experiments/baseline-rac/, plus the frozen *.variants.ts recovered from git HEAD into experiments/baseline-variants/) against the rewritten files.

The unit counted is a Tailwind utility whose variant chain contains at least one interaction-state condition. Structural variants (size, orientation, motion-reduce, descendant selectors) are excluded: nothing about them changes with the engine.

FOCUS_RING and FOCUS_RING_SELF are constants rather than literals, so both are expanded to the two utilities they emit before counting — otherwise the WCAG 2.4.7 ring would score zero in the two components where losing it was the headline defect.
Comments and import statements are stripped before counting. A header paragraph explaining why a selector moved must not be scored as a use of it.
method.proof: packages/ui/src/state-vocabulary.test.tsx — 42 assertions, each pinning BOTH that the engine puts the state where this table says AND that the element's class string carries a rule keyed to it. Verified by mutation: reverting toggle's ON state, switch's checked state or checkbox's focus ring each turns the suite red.

the_mapping_table.$note: kind is the honest description of the edit, and it is the field that matters. 'rename' is scriptable. 'pseudo-class' is scriptable but costs test coverage. 'resubject' means the name was right and the ELEMENT moved — the failure mode a name-keyed script cannot see. 'workaround' means no attribute exists on the target element at all. 'NONE' means the state does not exist anywhere in the library.

data-hovered.evidence: grep -rl 'data-hovered' over the whole installed @base-ui/react@1.7.0 dist returns 0 files. Confirmed by render: probe.state-vocabulary.json entries button.hover, tabs.hover, numberField.hover and switch.hover carry no new attribute after pointerenter/mouseenter/mouseover.
data-hovered.trap: The library DOES ship a data-hovering, so a grep for 'hover' finds a plausible-looking hit. It belongs to ScrollArea.Scrollbar alone (scroll-area/scrollbar/ScrollAreaScrollbarDataAttributes.mjs:10) and means the scroll area is hovered. It is not a general hover state and cannot substitute for one.
data-hovered.cost: Loses the unit tier. jsdom models no pointer, so matches(':hover') is permanently false — measured in probe3.testability.json. Under React Aria the same state was an attribute and fully assertable.
data-hovered.do_not_apply_blindly: On menu, select and combobox ITEMS the correct answer is data-highlighted, not :hover. Base UI drives one focus cursor for pointer and keyboard alike, so adding a hover rule there fights the arrow keys.

data-pressed (React Aria's transient poi.evidence: button/ButtonDataAttributes declares 'disabled' and nothing else. probe.state-vocabulary.json → button.pressed carries no attribute after pointerdown/mousedown.
data-pressed (React Aria's transient poi.fidelity: PARTIAL, and the difference is a real gesture. React Aria computed a press STATE that survived the pointer leaving and returning and covered a held Space. :active is the platform's and ends when the pointer leaves. Press, drag off, drag back: React Aria stayed lit, this does not.
data-pressed (React Aria's transient poi.cost: Same lost unit tier as hover: matches(':active') is permanently false in jsdom.

data-selected (on a Toggle).kind: rename, but see below — this is the single most dangerous row in the table
data-selected (on a Toggle).evidence: toggle/ToggleDataAttributes declares pressed and disabled only. probe.state-vocabulary.json → toggle.on shows data-pressed on a control no pointer is touching.
data-selected (on a Toggle).why_it_is_dangerous: The two libraries use the SAME NAME for OPPOSITE states. React Aria's data-pressed is the transient pointer-down; Base UI's is the persistent ON state. Every other row in this table fails LOUDLY when applied backwards — the selector stops matching. This one fails QUIETLY in both directions: applied backwards you get a toggle that flashes under the finger and forgets, which reviews as a working control.
data-selected (on a Toggle).aggravating_factor: toggle-group.tsx is still on React Aria and still means React Aria's thing by data-selected. Two files in one tree, one word, two meanings.

data-selected (on a Tab).evidence: grep of tabs/ finds no data-selected at all. probe2.state-vocabulary.json → tabs.selected-is-b shows data-active on the tab whose aria-selected is true.
data-selected (on a Tab).trap: data-composite-item-active travels separately as the roving-focus cursor. Styling that one instead underlines whichever tab the arrow keys last passed over rather than the one whose panel is showing — visible only to a keyboard user arrowing without activating.

data-selected (on a Select or ComboBox i.evidence: select/item/SelectItemDataAttributes and combobox/item/ComboboxItemDataAttributes both declare it. probe2.state-vocabulary.json → select.open.items shows it on the option whose aria-selected is true.
data-selected (on a Select or ComboBox i.why_it_matters: This row is why a blanket ban on React Aria's vocabulary would be the wrong migration instrument. data-selected is dead on toggle, dead on tabs, and alive here. The per-component tests exist for exactly this.

data-selected (on a Checkbox or Switch).evidence: probe.state-vocabulary.json → switch.on, checkbox.on. Both attributes land on the ROOT (the visible box / track), not on the wrapping label React Aria used.
data-selected (on a Checkbox or Switch).why_resubject: Both halves of the selector change. Renaming data-selected to data-checked while keeping the group- prefix produces a rule that still addresses the label, which never carries it. Base UI writes data-filled on the label in the checked state, which is Field's 'has a value' state and a tempting wrong answer.

data-indeterminate.kind: resubject — SAME NAME, and it still needed an edit
data-indeterminate.evidence: probe.state-vocabulary.json → checkbox.indeterminate: the attribute is on the root, not the label.
data-indeterminate.why_it_matters: This is the row that breaks name-keyed migration scripts. A table matching on names alone marks it 'no change' and ships a checkbox that never shows a dash. The subject moved even though the word did not.

data-focus-visible.evidence: grep -rl 'data-focus-visible' over the whole dist returns 0 files.
data-focus-visible.the_near_miss: Base UI publishes data-focused from Field.Root (field/root/FieldRoot.mjs:46), and it is the WRONG state to hang a ring on: it is set from plain focus with no modality filter, so a ring built on it appears on a mouse click. That is the defect :focus-visible was standardised to remove.
data-focus-visible.what_made_it_easy: Base UI inverts React Aria's arrangement. Checkbox.Root and Switch.Root are themselves the focusable element — role=checkbox / role=switch, tabindex=0 — while the hidden input is tabindex=-1 and aria-hidden. So the ring goes on the visible box directly and the group hop React Aria forced disappears. Measured: probe.state-vocabulary.json → checkbox.focus, switch.focus.
data-focus-visible.cost: Zero test coverage lost, uniquely among the pseudo-class rows: jsdom DOES match :focus-visible on a focused element (probe3.testability.json), so the WCAG 2.4.7 ring keeps its unit tier and state-vocabulary.test.tsx asserts it behaviourally.

data-focus-within.evidence: grep -rl 'data-focus-within' over the whole dist returns 0 files.
data-focus-within.used_by: combobox — React Aria wrote it on its Group wrapper to move the border when the inner input took focus.

data-focused (on a collection item).evidence: probe.state-vocabulary.json → select.open, menu.open, combobox.open. Same behaviour: one focus cursor driven for pointer and keyboard alike, exactly as React Aria's was.

data-open (on a trigger).evidence: probe2.state-vocabulary.json → select.open.trigger. The trigger also gains data-pressed and data-popup-side while open.
data-open (on a trigger).note: data-open still exists in Base UI, on the POPUP rather than the trigger. So this rename is also a resubject if it is applied without looking at which element the rule sits on.

data-entering.evidence: grep -rl 'data-entering' returns 0 files; data-starting-style is declared across dialog/, popover/, tooltip/, select/, menu/, combobox/ and observed at mount in probe.state-vocabulary.json → select.open, menu.open, combobox.open.
data-entering.note: The meaning survives intact — a one-frame 'before' style the transition runs away from. Base UI's name mirrors the CSS @starting-style rule.

data-exiting.evidence: Same grep and the same dist declarations as data-entering.

data-[placement=…].evidence: grep -rl 'data-placement' returns 0 files. probe2.state-vocabulary.json → popover.parts and tooltip.parts show the popup carrying data-side and data-align as two attributes.
data-[placement=…].why_it_is_not_a_rename: React Aria's single value carried both axes. Lumo's two rules happen to need only the side half, so the split cost nothing here — but a rule keyed to an ALIGNED placement would have to become two conditions, and a rename script would silently emit a selector that matches nothing.
data-[placement=…].counted_as: rename, because that is what it was in these two files. The caveat is recorded rather than averaged away.

data-dragging.evidence: slider/thumb/SliderThumbDataAttributes.mjs:9 and slider/root/SliderRootDataAttributes.mjs:5. Confirmed under a simulated pointer drag: probe2.state-vocabulary.json → slider.during-drag shows it on the thumb, the track, the indicator and the root.
data-dragging.why_it_matters: Together with data-disabled reaching every slider part, this is the whole reason slider scored ZERO rewrites — the only component in the thirteen that did.

data-disabled.kind: no change, and the widest-reaching state in the library
data-disabled.evidence: Measured on every one of the thirteen. It reaches the label AND the control on checkbox and switch; the input, the group and both steppers on number-field; the track, indicator, thumb and output on slider; the button on button and toggle; items on menu, select and tabs.
data-disabled.share_of_survivors: Of the 28 state utilities that carried over unchanged across the thirteen, the large majority are data-disabled rules.

data-invalid.base_ui_equivalent: data-invalid, but its REACH is per-component
data-invalid.kind: resubject on checkbox; WORKAROUND on number-field
data-invalid.evidence: probe.state-vocabulary.json → checkbox.invalid puts it on the root span, the label and the error text. numberField.invalid puts it on the root and on NOTHING else — not the input, not the group, not the steppers.
data-invalid.why_the_difference: Base UI publishes validity onto a control when that control sits inside a Field.Root and the FIELD decides it is invalid. NumberField.Root is not a Field.Root and Base UI's number field has no invalid prop, so Lumo writes the attribute by hand onto the root and it goes no further.
data-invalid.the_workaround: A named group on NumberField.Root and a group rule on the input. A rename could not fix it: there is no attribute on the input to rename TO.

data-placeholder.evidence: probe.state-vocabulary.json → select.closed shows it on both the trigger and the value span.

genuine_workarounds.$definition: An edit that could not be expressed as a rename or a pseudo-class swap because the state does not appear on the element the rule has to sit on. These are the ones a migration script cannot do and a human has to think about.

cases.problem: The tick and dash glyphs are Lumo's own lucide icons, not Base UI parts, so they receive no state attributes at all — measured: probe.state-vocabulary.json → checkbox.on, elements 4 and 6 carry no data attribute.
cases.why_the_obvious_fix_was_rejected: Base UI's own answer is <Checkbox.Indicator>, which mounts conditionally. Adopting it swaps CSS toggling for a conditional mount and reflows the box between states, which is what the always-rendered pair was chosen to avoid.
cases.fix: A NAMED group on Checkbox.Root, read by the two icons. Named rather than bare because the label above is already an unnamed group and a bare group variant binds to whichever ancestor is nearest.
cases.asymmetry_worth_noting: switch.tsx needed NO such workaround for the identical shape of rule, because Switch.Thumb IS a Base UI part and Base UI propagates the checked state onto it. Which parts carry which state is per-component knowledge that cannot be derived from a mapping table. That is the finding.

cases.problem: data-invalid reaches the root only. See the data-invalid row above.
cases.fix: A named group on NumberField.Root, read by the input.

adjacent_forced_edits_not_counted_in_the.$note: Real edits the migration forces that are not state selectors, so they are excluded from the headline count rather than quietly folded in.

anchor_width_variable.was: the React Aria custom property naming the measured trigger width
anchor_width_variable.now: Base UI's own custom property, written by its positioner
anchor_width_variable.why: The variable name is engine-owned. Keeping the old one silently shrink-wraps the panel — a layout defect with no error.

focus_ring_constant_fork.what: FOCUS_RING_SELF added beside FOCUS_RING rather than replacing it, because radio-group.tsx and rating.tsx are still React Aria and still need the group form.
focus_ring_constant_fork.cost: A library mid-migration carries both spellings of its own focus ring. That is the shape of a partial migration, and it is a maintenance hazard for as long as it lasts.

button.what: 4 hover rules and 4 press rules to pseudo-classes. data-disabled untouched. The focus ring needed no edit at all: Base UI's Button renders a real <button>, Lumo marks it, and theme.css's :focus-visible rule was never engine-specific.

toggle.what: 2 hover rules to :hover, 3 ON-state rules from data-selected to data-pressed. The most dangerous rename in the table.

switch.what: 1 hover to a group-hover, 5 checked rules resubjected off the label onto the track and thumb, 2 focus-ring rules to :focus-visible on the track itself.

checkbox.what: Worst case. Every state moved off the label onto the root; 2 focus-ring rules; 3 icon rules that needed the named-group workaround. Only data-disabled on the label survived.

slider.what: ZERO. data-dragging and data-disabled are spelled the same and reach the same parts. The only component in the thirteen the engine swap did not touch.

number-field.what: 3 hover rules, 1 validity rule that needed the named-group workaround. All 4 disabled rules survived.

select.what: 1 hover, 1 focus cursor to data-highlighted, 1 open state to data-popup-open.

menu.what: 1 focus cursor to data-highlighted, 1 submenu open state to data-popup-open.

combobox.what: 1 hover, 1 focus-within to the pseudo-class, 1 focus cursor to data-highlighted.

dialog.what: Every selector in the file is a transition selector, so nothing survived. Six clean renames.

popover.what: 4 transition renames plus 2 placement rules that are a split rather than a rename.

extrapolation_to_77.why_not_mean_times_77: The thirteen were chosen as the core INTERACTIVE set, so they are the state-heaviest components in the library by construction. 5.15 × 77 = 397 would price a badge and a spinner at five rewrites each — a fabricated number wearing a decimal point.
extrapolation_to_77.what_was_done_instead: The same census was run over all 77 registry ui items, reading the thirteen from their React Aria baseline so the population is uniformly pre-migration. Only the RATE is extrapolated.

date_family_excluded_figure.why_excluded: Base UI ships zero primitives for this family (base-vega-coverage.json → the_date_family.base_ui_proper_primitives: 0). Its 44 state selectors are not migrated, they are authored fresh alongside an interaction layer nobody has built. Counting them as renames would price the library's largest unknown at a few find-and-replaces.

extrapolation_to_77.the_number_to_quote_explained: 179 selector rewrites across the 71 components that have a migration path at all, of which roughly 15% of AFFECTED components will need a structural workaround rather than a rename. calendar alone carries 44 more that are a build, not a migration.

confidence_and_limits: The 70.5% rewrite rate is measured on thirteen components and applied to sixty-four. The thirteen are more state-dense per component but there is no reason to think their MIX of state kinds is unrepresentative — hover, focus, selected, disabled and transitions are the same five ideas everywhere. Still: it is a rate, not a census, for 64 of the 77.

The count is of SELECTORS, not of engineer-hours. A rename found by grep and a resubject that requires knowing which element carries the state cost very different amounts, which is why the kind field exists and why the workaround count is reported separately.
34 of the 77 have zero state selectors and cost nothing on this axis. They are not free overall — they still need their imports and their tests moved — but this particular number does not touch them.

TEST COST IS NOT IN THIS NUMBER. Every existing test that asserts a state attribute has to be rewritten too. Lumo has exactly one such test today — toggle.test.tsx — which is itself the finding: nothing in the suite caught a frozen switch, an unstyled checkbox or a dead focus ring across four rounds. Building the coverage that WOULD catch it is a cost this migration should be charged for, and packages/ui/src/state-vocabulary.test.tsx is 42 assertions covering thirteen components as the first instalment.

toggle.test.tsx now FAILS on this branch, correctly: it asserts data-selected for an ON toggle, which is React Aria's vocabulary. It was left failing rather than weakened. The failure is the engine-specific test tax made visible.

Hover and press lose their unit tier entirely on this engine — jsdom models no pointer, measured in probe3.testability.json. Those two states move to a browser or visual tier or they are not verified at all. The focus ring does NOT lose it, which is the one place this migration got lucky.
